The proposed Pythagorean and segment-calculation scopes fit this method, with rectangle properties supporting EF = BC.

audits.mathematicalReason: Angle sums give ∠ADB = 120° and ∠ADC = 60°. Normalize BD = 1 and CD = 2, and drop AH perpendicular to BC. Write BH = AH = h, using ∠ABH = 45°. Then DH = h − 1 and h = sqrt(3)(h − 1), so h = (3 + sqrt(3))/2. Consequently CH = 3 − h > 0, and tan(∠ACB) = h/(3 − h) = 2 + sqrt(3) = tan(45° + 30°). The angle is acute, hence 75°. The synthetic route is also defensible: let M be the midpoint of DC and construct equilateral DME on A's side of BC, so E lies on AD. Isosceles BDE and SAS congruence of BDE and CME give BE = CE and ∠ECD = 30°. The two 15° angles in ABE give AE = BE. Also EC is perpendicular to AD, so AEC is isosceles right and ∠ACE = 45°. Thus ∠ACB = 45° + 30° = 75°. Both route node sets have genuine mathematical uses; their union is not required.
